brief_extract:
THE EAW STORY
by MARY GEORGE, CBE, Companion IEE, Director EAW

IN this Golden Jubilee year of the EAW when we are so much in the news people often ask how our Association came to be started. Our story began in a Mayfair drawing room on November 12, 1924 at 4.30 p.m. The occasion was an informal tea party at the home of Sir Charles and Lady Parsons and the guests included a number of distinguished men and women prominent in electrical and other fields.

brief_extract:
To avoid confusion with another organisation with the same initials "WEA" the title was altered to the present one with the now well-known initials "EAW". First branch
The first branch of the EAW was formed in Glasgow in November 1925. Birmingham, Manchester and Newcastle-upon-Tyne quickly followed suit and by 1928 the Association was so well established, together with its journal "The Electrical Age" founded in 1926, that it was referred to by Dr Ferranti in his Faraday Lecture that year in the following words:
"Most happily there has arisen a new great force in the Electrical Association for Women.

brief_extract:
The War and after
The 1939/45 war put a brake on branch development but power cuts, restriction of supplies and shortages of equipment placed increased value on the work of existing branches in educating and informing people on the economical use of electricity. The reward came in 1945 at a time of national rejoicing for peace when the Association was able to celebrate its 21st birthday with a big exhibition in London and a symposium of speeches at the Institution of Electrical Engineers. The original Caroline Haslett Trust was also established in that year.

article_title: The cost of electricity in the home
brief_extract: Electricity is not the only victim of price changes. Oil prices have gone up too and as a result the Greater London Council have had to propose an increase of 55% on oil-based heating in council flats. In electricity tariffs the three broad components are the customer-related cost; the energy cost (or the cost of shovelling more coal on the boilers); and the capital cost (or cost related to demand) which means having to build more and bigger power stations.

brief_context: Comparing domestic electricity prices with those in Europe.
article_title: The cost of electricity in the home
brief_extract: Even allowing for increased charges from January 1975 every domestic customer will still be underpaying by over £10 a year for the electricity used in a bill of between £45 and £50. Yet when charges are adjusted electricity in this country will still be amongst the lowest priced in Europe. The Industry's heritage is a substantial take-over of energy in the home by the year 2000.

Here then are a few suggestions. Gardens to visit
If you live in the South some well known
gardens come to mind: RHS Gardens at Wisley
—near the village of Ripley and just off the A3
(London—Portsmouth road); Leonardslee south
of Horsham on the A281 close by the hamlet
of Crabtree, a spectacular display of camellias,
azaleas and rhododendrons; then there is
Wakehurst which besides magnolias, pieris, and

sisting of over 300 species—Wakehurst is just
north of Ardingly on the B2028 (quite close to
the Sussex Showground). Gun Hill Place,

the A12, is open only on certain Sundays in the
spring so it is advisable to check before you go.

brief_context: Location of a boiler factory where Caroline Haslett worked.
brief_extract: It was this genius for co-operation which brought the EAW into contact with so many other organisations and gained widespread recognition of the value of its purpose. As the first Secretary of the Women’s Engineering Society, the EAW’s parent, and with a background of work in a Scottish boiler factory in the First World War, Caroline Haslett had an understanding of precision methods and of time and motion study and thus the EAW was one of the first organisations to take an interest in kitchen planning and in scientific management in the home. At a time when women were only just emerging into public life Caroline Haslett saw the value of men and women working together and she was often the first woman to hold the many appointments that were offered in varied spheres where her administrative gifts and her understanding of human beings were, recognised.

brief_context: Where Caroline Haslett served as a Justice of the Peace.
brief_extract: In 1931 she was made a Commander of the Order of the British Empire and in 1947 became a Dame Commander of this Order. She was a Justice of the Peace for the County of London. MARY GEORGE, CBE, BA, Companion IEE, succeeded Dame Caroline in 1956.

brief_context: One of three most used electrical systems mentioned.
brief_extract: Just as the 13A plug and socket outlet has, over the past 28 years, become accepted as the standard for use on new and rewired domestic installations in this country, to the virtual exclusion of other types, so other countries throughout the world have developed independently their own plugs and socket outlets, all having quite different dimensions and arrangement of pins. The three most used systems are those of the UK, the USA and a design known as the ‘Europlug’ which is used in most European countries. These three systems are not mutually compatible and a hazard could arise if, for instance, attempts are made to use an imported appliance fitted with, say, a ‘Europlug’ by inserting it into a British socket outlet.

brief_extract: How did this come about? Lady Hornsby-Smith: I was secretary to the Development Manager, and later the Development Director, of the Central London Electricity Company - this was before nationalisation of course - and I entered for the competition as the result of a wager. When the head of all the showrooms was talking about entering some of his demonstrators my boss said: 'I bet my secretary can beat all of them'.

brief_extract: Years later when I was a judge at the National Final of this Competition I was able to assure the contestants that I knew exactly how they felt. Miss George: I believe you know the United States well and I noticed from your biographical notes that you were given a State Department Grant in 1953. What did this entail?

location_entry: Headquarters of the American Medical Association
brief_context: Where she was lambasted as promoting socialised medicine.
article_title: BARONESS HORNSBY-SMITH in an interview by MISS MARY GEORGE
brief_extract: Since I was at the Ministry of Health I chose to study the hospital and welfare services from coast to coast. At that time I was lambasted as promoting 'socialised medicine' and at a luncheon at the Headquarters of the American Medical Association the walls were plastered with posters stating that 'Socialised Medicine was the first step on the slippery slope to Communism.' I shall always remember with gratitude the stand for free speech made by Harvard University when they invited me to address the Medical School on the British National Health Service. All this was in the period which led up to Macarthyism, but since then the States have introduced their own Medicare scheme.

brief_context: Location of the Golden Jubilee Conference.
brief_extract:
Ouwehand-Hartree of the Dutch EAW

THE Golden Jubilee Conference was the climax of a year in which the EAW Branches had celebrated the 50 years of the Association's work in many varied ways which not only afforded pleasure and interest in the event but presented the EAW's continuing value in times when consumer organisations have a vital importance. From May 6th to 8th representatives from the 260 branches met in London to enjoy conference sessions and social gatherings and a very friendly start to the whole conference was given by the 'At Home' at EAW Headquarters. Reception at Guildhall
At an evening reception in historic Guildhall in the City of London HRH Princess Alice, Duchess of Gloucester, graciously cut the EAW birthday cake designed in the form of an all-electric house with the title 'The Watts, 50 Golden Way, EAW 1'.

Lady De La Warr made the following statement
on VAT and the power tools of the housewife:—
‘We are angry with the Chancellor of the Ex-
chequer for classing such labour-saving domestic
appliances as washing machines, refrigerators
and vacuum cleaners as luxuries in his budget and
subjecting them to a savage increase in VAT. These are after all the power tools of the house-
wife and are absolutely essential to women who
have to go out to work and also run a home, and
yet men’s tools such as electric drills and saws
which they need to help them with their work are
exempt from the higher tax.

article_title: Hospitality to EAW Members from Overseas
brief_extract:
Hospitality to EAW Members from Overseas
Many branches and individual members have
continuing association with the EAW in the
Netherlands, New Zealand, and Trinidad and
Tobago, and members from Britain have been
welcomed by the EAW in these three countries. The two representatives each from Holland
and New Zealand were here for a very short time
but the large contingent from Trinidad and
Tobago had a longer stay in London, and Lon-
don Branch and Enfield Branch did them signal
honour. A special coffee morning was arranged
at the home of Mrs Gilbert, London Branch
Chairman, and so much interest was aroused in
members that the branch arranged a visit to the
Commonwealth Institute to see the Trinidad,
Tobago and New Zealand exhibits.

brief_context: Used to illustrate extreme low relative humidity levels.
brief_extract:
The Case For Humidifiers

THE more efficient the heating system in the home the greater the need for humidification to restore the correct level of moisture in the air. In centrally heated premises without humidification the relative humidity is usually found to be about 20%, equivalent to the level in the Sahara Desert. This is well below the recommended range of 50-55% relative humidity which is the level suitable for normal indoor temperatures of about 70°F.

brief_context: Region where new ceramic safety regulations apply
brief_extract:
In providing the consumer with information,
standards were required particularly those speci-
fying minimum safety requirements and they had
to be amended as quickly as unforeseen difficul-
ties arose or as the goods themselves were modi-
fied. Glazed Ceramic Ware
The Glazed Ceramic Ware (Safety) Regula-
tions 1975 has introduced safeguards to limit
the lead and cadmium release allowed in glazed
ceramic ware offered for sale in Great Britain
and to ensure that it cannot contaminate food
to a harmful degree. They came into force on
October 1st for sales by manufacturers and im-
porters and will operate from February 1, 1976,
for sales by wholesalers and retailers.

brief_context: Location of the salmon hatchery.
article_title: VISIT TO CEGB CYNRIG SALMON HATCHERY
brief_extract: Brecon, in the lush valley of the Usk, in the centre of a National Park has an irresistible appeal to anglers and has been known for generations as an angling centre. The CEGB has played its part in contributing to Brecon’s fine angling heritage by providing a salmon hatchery on Llanfrynach on the River Cynrig, an Usk tributary. One of the hatchery’s major roles is to ensure that, when taking water from the River Usk as part of the process of generating power, the Board not only does not hinder the salmon, but has instituted a programme research in which certain aspects of the life of young salmon in rivers, and the use of hatcheries in improving salmon stocks, are being studied.

brief_context: Tags from salmon have been returned from this coast.
article_title: VISIT TO CEGB CYNRIG SALMON HATCHERY
brief_extract:
Smolts released from the hatchery are marked with numbered tags in the hope that fishermen or anglers who subsequently catch the adult fish will return the tags to the hatchery since in this way the scientific knowledge of salmon will be increased, thus providing a basis for decisions on the best way of stocking rivers. Tags have been returned from fish caught as far afield as the coasts of Greenland and Western Ireland as well as nearer home in the River Usk system. CONSERVATION OF ENERGY EXHIBITION
